title: CPlane / Routing / Auth — Firebreak standup notes (2027-11-02)
content:
Attendees: Marcus, Anita, Priya, Ethan, Jordan (brief), ops-oncall (joined 10:15)
Goal: quick sync pre-firebreak — validate routing fallthroughs, auth token refresh behavior, and quota signal gating before weekend maintenance window. Keep items lightweight; capture blockers and owners.

1) Quick wins / resolves since last sync
- Fixed race in allocator when a retired pool reported zero capacity; root cause: stale heartbeat not cleaned before route reassignment (PR #1423). Deployed to staging, smoke passed.
- Auth refresh jitter reduced by moving refresh scheduling to pooled worker (Anita). Observed ~10% reduction in refresh storms on heavy-tenancy customers.

2) Current risks we need to watch for firebreak
- Quota signal lag: metrics show 45–60s delay for quota counters under bursty traffic from the sandbox cluster. Impact: customers can exceed realtime quotas briefly causing bursts of throttles. Mitigation: short-term — increase sampling frequency for quota-aggregator to 5s; long-term — migrate to streaming counter (JIRA-QUOTA-1291). Owner: Priya (action: run perf-run tonight, report 11/03).
- Auth token edge case: token refresh failures for cross-region requests when KMS rotation overlaps refresh window. Repro steps in ticket JIRA-PLTFM-873. Ops will schedule a canary rotate tomorrow morning. Owner: Anita + Ops.

3) Routing fallbacks and policy testing
- Canary routing policy for low-latency clients validated: requests that hit overloaded pools are retried to secondary pool with preserved KV-cache hint. Need to confirm KV cache warm-up cost; initial numbers show a 12% median latency increase for first token after reroute. Action: Ethan to prototype a prefix cache clone on reroute to reduce cold miss. ETA: 11/10.
- Fallthrough metrics: add a 'reroute-reason' tag to traces so we can correlate with quota hits and model variant downgrades. Owner: Marcus.

4) Action items (concrete)
- Priya: run surge soak with synthetic clients (50k qps peak) against quota-aggregator change; attach flamegraphs and histogram to JIRA-QUOTA-1291. Due 2027-11-03 EOD.
- Anita: coordinate canary KMS rotation with ops; capture timing windows and rollback plan. Due 2027-11-04 AM.
- Ethan: spike draft for cache-clone-on-reroute (prototype + perf microbench). Due 2027-11-10.
- Marcus: add reroute-reason tag to tracing pipeline and update dashboard panel. Due 2027-11-05.
- Jordan: prepare short runbook excerpt for oncall describing common reroute signatures and remediation steps. Due 2027-11-03.

5) Blockers / open questions
- Capacity prediction heuristic is still overshooting for short tail spikes — does the allocator need a burst-tier separate from reserved pools? Discussion: likely yes, but need cost model. Suggest a short spike-tier design doc. (Owner: platform-alloc team, nomination: Marcus).
- How do we prioritize rollback if a quota aggregator change causes false positives? Do we automate rollback based on error-rate > 3% for 2m? Ops to propose safe thresholds.

6) Notes to self / informal thoughts (scratchpad)
- Quick experiments: try enabling counter sampling at 2.5s in staging to see tail behavior; if memory overhead is acceptable, use 5s in prod as intermediate.
- Consider tagging heavy tenants so we can route them off the shared burst path during maintenance windows. Might be a config flag per-customer in routing policy.
- Prompt for next sync: show 'reroute cost' histogram across 3 customer segments + impact on token spend.

7) Post-meeting follow-ups (short log)
- 10:40 — ops confirmed staging canary for KMS rotation scheduled 11/03 02:00 UTC; will monitor for 30m then decide.
- 11:05 — Priya started perf-run on quota-aggregator with synthetic spikes; initial result: sampling at 5s reduced latency of counter aggregation by ~22% but CPU increased by ~8%. Priya to analyze if CPU increase is sustainable for prod fleet.

8) Decisions made
- Short-term: enable 5s sampling on quota-aggregator for weekend firebreak; rollback plan in case of CPU > 12% increase or error-rate > 0.8%.
- Medium-term: schedule spike-tier design doc and cost model for Q1 planning.

Meeting end: 11:20 — next check-in if any emergent issue during firebreak at 11/03 02:45 UTC.

-- scratch notes (rough) --
- "todo: verify whether client SDK retry backoff needs to be adjusted when we do reroutes to avoid double-retries"
- "question: can we surface reroute count to customer analytics? maybe as opt-in"

Raw refs: JIRA-PLTFM-873, JIRA-QUOTA-1291, GH PR 1423, Confluence Routing+Quota Epics

End of notes.
